newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones family member says not giving up.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones family member says not giving up.

text.p: William Cox III, a member of the family that controls Dow Jones & Co Inc, said Friday he resigned from the company for a variety of reasons, but still plans to pursue efforts to make Dow Jones more profitable.
"There's a lot of value at Dow Jones, but I think it has to be unlocked," Cox said in an interview with Reuters.
But he said the overriding reasons he decided to leave the company are "personal," as well as financial, maintaining he could make three times as much elsewhere.
"I've got a lot of offers," Cox said, declining to name his options.
Cox said he gave his two weeks' notice. His last day is February 21 at Dow Jones, where he manages the company's global stock indexes.

Cox's father, William Cox Jr, is a Dow Jones board member. While the younger Cox and his cousin, Elisabeth Goth, have made headlines in recent weeks discussing their disappointment with the company's direction and the value of its stock, the elder Cox and other members of the family have said they support the company's management.
The younger Cox said he has not "deviated at all" from his quest to increase shareholder value at Dow Jones.

Dow Jones' stock took a hit in late January after the company reported it would spend $650 million to expand and revitalize its Telerate financial information services unit. On the day of that announcement, the company's stock fell 4-1/2 points to 36-3/8.
It has since recovered slightly, closing at 39-5/8 on Friday.

A Dow Jones spokesman earlier in the day confirmed rumors Cox had resigned. But the spokesman, citing privacy rules governing personnel matters, would not disclose the reasons given or the effective date of his resignation.
